--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.get_edge_df()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.get_edge_df()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Get edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. title: >- [Graph.get_edge_df()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27386-L27470){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge DataFrame](../assets/graphs/get-edge-df.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph with node ids 1 to 4 on the nodes and edge ids 1 to 5 on the edges. The result is a table with the columns id, source, target, and rel: one row per edge sorted by id, with endpoints given as node ids and rel empty (null)." width="100%"} Returns all edges with a consistent column structure: - column 1: `id` (i64, mandatory, sorted ascending) - column 2: `source` (i64, mandatory) - column 3: `target` (i64, mandatory) - column 4: `rel` (str, mandatory, null if not set) - columns 5-N: Other attributes (alphabetically sorted) - weight is included as a special attribute if present The DataFrame is always sorted by edge ID in ascending order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A Polars DataFrame with edges sorted by `id`. If the graph has no edges, the frame has no rows but still has the `id`, `source`, `target` and `rel` columns (and `weight` on a weighted graph). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The layout mirrors `get_node_df()` in spirit: `id`, `source`, `target`, and `rel` always come first (in that order), followed by `weight` and any other custom edge attributes in alphabetical order, with rows sorted by `id` ascending. `weight` is treated as a first-class attribute column rather than a bare number so it can be filtered and aggregated with the rest of the schema. Missing `rel` values appear as `None`. Attributes whose values differ in type from edge to edge are reconciled as in `get_node_df()`. The `id`, `source` and `target` columns always hold the edge IDs and endpoints, so an attribute with one of those names is left out of the table, and so is a `weight` attribute when any edge has a weight (`get_edge_attrs()` reads them). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every edge DataFrame starts with `id`, `source`, `target`, and `rel`, followed by `weight` and any other custom attributes: ::: {#c81490d2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B", 1.5, {"rel": "friend"}), ("B", "C", 2.0, {"rel": "colleague"}), ("C", "D", 1.0, {"rel": "friend"}), ] ) ) df = graph.get_edge_df() df.columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['id', 'source', 'target', 'rel', 'weight'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#53062b1e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 5) ``` ::: ::: Being a regular Polars DataFrame, it supports the usual filtering and aggregation -- for example, isolating edges of a given relationship type: ::: {#9ef46294 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl df.filter(pl.col("rel") == "friend") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 5)
idsourcetargetrelweight
i64i64i64strf64
112"friend"1.5
334"friend"1.0
``` ::: ::: Or grouping to count how many edges fall into each relationship type: ::: {#6db97bad .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.group_by("rel").len() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 2)
rellen

``` ::: ::: Aggregating `weight` per group works the same way as with any Polars DataFrame: ::: {#4ea05ef2 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.group_by("rel").agg(pl.col("weight").mean()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: :::
